# DSP reference fixture

`dsp-reference.txt` is generated by `tests/reference/dsp_oracle.c` against ciglet commit `895ba9b1c0eabee83d3544208bbc82420efa3206`, with GCC on Ubuntu x86_64 and `-DFP_TYPE=float -std=c99`, linking `-lm`. Values are printed with nine significant digits to preserve binary32 results on round-trip parsing.

This fixture checks vector statistics, six precise window functions, and frame padding. A maximum absolute error of `1e-7` passes the current Windows MSVC x86_64 and i686 comparisons. This is a scoped threshold for these inputs, not a tolerance claim covering all DSP algorithms or all input sizes.

Compile with `gcc -DFP_TYPE=float -std=c99 -I<upstream> tests/reference/dsp_oracle.c -lm -o dsp-oracle`, then capture `dsp-oracle` output. The fixture does not require linking the upstream library because these tested reference functions are inline definitions in `ciglet.h`.

Intentional corrections: empty statistical inputs return errors or `None`; invalid vector sizes return errors; singleton windows are unity instead of dividing by zero; sorting uses deterministic total ordering and preserves the original index order of equal values.

The FFT fixtures c-fft-f32.bin and c-fft-f64.bin use the pinned unmodified ciglet.c and external/fftsg_h.c compiled with FP_TYPE=float and FP_TYPE=double respectively. tests/reference/fft_oracle.c writes 240 records and 92,112 scalar outputs per precision. Cases cover lengths 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 256, 512, and 1024; impulses, deterministic complex signals, and large DC offsets; all four present/absent real/imaginary combinations; and both transform directions. The C build uses -O2 -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections -lm, without -Ofast or fast-math. Section removal allows unused ciglet subsystems to remain unlinked. No upstream source is modified.

Binary format: ASCII FFT1, little-endian uint32 scalar byte width and record count, then uint32 length/scenario/component-mask/inverse fields per record followed by interleaved real/imaginary scalars. This fixture is generated on Ubuntu x86_64, whose native byte order is little-endian; Rust decodes it explicitly.

Across Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686, all eight integration tests pass. Maximum absolute differences across these targets are 2.288818359375e-5 for f32 and 1.1368683772161603e-13 for f64. Errors normalized by max(1, maximum input component magnitude) times length for forward transforms, or by the same input magnitude for normalized inverse transforms, were at most 3.3527612686157227e-8 and 1.1102230246251565e-16 respectively. Acceptance thresholds are 2e-7 for f32 and 1e-15 for f64, allowing platform/backend variation while remaining close to measured errors. These are scoped kernel thresholds, not complete speech-feature or inference tolerances. Independent round-trip and Parseval checks validate normalization; frequency-shift checks cover odd/even/singleton/empty sequences against the original inline ordering.

The direct inverse DFT fixtures c-idft-f32.bin and c-idft-f64.bin use tests/reference/idft_oracle.c with the same pinned unmodified C source and compiler flags as the FFT oracle. A reproducible POSIX command from the crate root is shown below; set CIGLET_UPSTREAM to the pinned checkout and repeat with FP_TYPE=double for the f64 fixture. The IDF1 format uses the same field layout as FFT1, with 120 records and 3,552 scalar outputs per precision. Lengths 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 11, 16, 31, and 64 include non-power-of-two and prime cases, with the same three input families and four component-presence combinations. Every record uses the normalized inverse convention. Independent tests verify constant-spectrum cancellation, the positive imaginary sign of a known four-point inverse, all-zero absent inputs, and invalid shape/length errors. This implementation retains quadratic complexity and scalar arithmetic order; the FFT API remains available for power-of-two lengths.

```sh
gcc -O2 -DFP_TYPE=float -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -I"$CIGLET_UPSTREAM" tests/reference/idft_oracle.c "$CIGLET_UPSTREAM/ciglet.c" "$CIGLET_UPSTREAM/external/fftsg_h.c" -Wl,--gc-sections -lm -o idft-oracle
./idft-oracle tests/fixtures/c-idft-f32.bin
```

Across the five required native targets, the tested f32 inverse DFT values match C exactly. The largest observed f64 absolute difference is 1.1368683772161603e-13, with normalized error 5.551115123125783e-17. Acceptance thresholds are 2e-7 for f32 and 1e-15 for f64, using max(1, maximum input component magnitude) as the inverse-transform scale. These thresholds apply only to the recorded direct inverse DFT cases.

The DCT fixtures c-dct-f32.bin and c-dct-f64.bin use tests/reference/dct_oracle.c, the pinned unmodified C source, and the same section-removal build flags as the inverse DFT driver. Substitute dct_oracle.c and the matching executable/fixture names in the command above. DCT1 begins with a scalar byte width and record count as little-endian uint32 values. Each of the 32 records contains uint32 length/scenario fields followed by real scalar coefficients. Lengths 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 16, 32, and 64 and four signal families yield 524 coefficients per precision. The families are impulses, deterministic signed values, a constant offset, and alternating signs. A final uint32 count of 12 precedes f32 angle/sine/cosine triples, including positive/negative zero and arguments up to magnitude 1000.

The upstream DCT uses fastapprox's f32 fastcosfull even with FP_TYPE=double. Replacing it with a standard-library cosine would change the transform. The Rust implementation retains these coefficients, sign-bit handling, range reduction, multiplication/addition order, and double-precision square-root normalization. The approximation gives cos(0) about 0.9999864; the constant-signal DC coefficient retains that deviation from an ideal orthonormal DCT. Small-angle sine/cosine comparisons against standard trigonometry have a measured maximum absolute error of about 3.96e-5 across 2,001 angles between -4*pi and 4*pi. The accuracy test bound is 1e-4 and does not claim accurate large-angle range reduction. Empty DCT inputs and nonfinite/out-of-range approximate-trigonometry arguments return errors instead of the C implementation's invalid indexing or float-to-int conversion.

Across Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686, every tested DCT coefficient and approximation bit pattern matches C exactly. All fifteen integration tests pass on each target. The kernel comparison thresholds are 2e-7 for f32 and 1e-15 for f64 after normalizing by max(1, maximum input magnitude) times sqrt(length). These are scoped DCT thresholds, not complete feature-extraction tolerances.

The CZT fixtures c-czt-f32.bin and c-czt-f64.bin use tests/reference/czt_oracle.c against the pinned unmodified ciglet.c and Ooura FFT source, with the same -O2 section-removal flags as the preceding drivers. Substitute the driver and output filenames in the inverse DFT command above. CZT1 begins with little-endian uint32 scalar byte width and record count. Each of 1,200 records contains uint32 length/scenario/component-mask/inverse fields, the angular step in the selected precision, and interleaved output real/imaginary scalars. The reference contains 64,320 scalar outputs per precision. Lengths 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 11, 16, 31, 64, and 127 include prime and non-power-of-two cases. Three input families and all four component-presence combinations are tested with both directions and five grids: 2*pi/n, zero, 0.125, -0.25, and 2*pi/(1.5*n).

The Rust plan caches the FFT of the symmetric chirp kernel and reuses its work and scratch storage. The transform_into operation allocates no buffers. Chirp phases retain C's double expression followed by FP_TYPE storage; convolution uses the original twice-next-power-of-two padding. An unnormalized inverse FFT permits post-chirp multiplication before division by padded length, preserving the original normalization order. Inverse CZT negates the step and additionally divides by the signal length, as in the upstream wrapper; this is a true inverse on orthogonal DFT grids, not on arbitrary grids. Independent tests compare ordinary DFT grids to FFT results and round trips, and arbitrary grids to direct complex sums. Plan reuse, absent inputs, shape errors leaving output unchanged, overflow, and invalid phase domains are covered.

Across the five required native targets, all nineteen integration tests pass. Maximum absolute differences are of 1.7385095357894897e-2 for f32 and 7.275957614183426e-11 for f64. Maximum normalized errors are 1.7879210911753935e-7 and 3.5518465287690634e-16. Normalization uses max(1, maximum input component magnitude) times signal length for forward transforms, or the same input magnitude for inverse transforms. Measured kernel thresholds are 5e-7 for f32 and 2e-15 for f64. Complete speech-feature and inference tolerances remain to be validated.

The synthesis fixtures c-synthesis-f32.bin and c-synthesis-f64.bin use tests/reference/synthesis_oracle.c against the pinned unmodified header and source, with the same -O2 section-removal flags as preceding drivers. Substitute the driver and executable/fixture filenames in the inverse DFT command above. SYN1 begins with little-endian uint32 scalar byte width and record count. Each of 48 records contains uint32 single/length/sample-rate/tone-count fields, frequency/amplitude/center-phase scalar triples for each tone, and the output samples. Lengths 2, 3, 5, 16, 31, 128, 512, and 1001 and six scenarios yield 10,188 samples per precision. Sample rates alternate between 16000 and 44100. Cases cover unit-amplitude original single-tone generation, negative frequency and amplitude, three ordered tones, DC/Nyquist components, and empty tone lists.

The scalar recurrence retains C's double step expression, FP_TYPE step/phase storage, double cosine and initial amplitude multiplication, and FP_TYPE recurrence and summation order. Only two previous samples per tone are stored; the original length-sized temporary waveform is unnecessary. Phase refers to sample floor(length/2), including odd lengths. Single-tone generation intentionally corrects the original ignored amplitude. Original single-tone C fixtures use only unit amplitude; independent centered cosine checks validate the correction for zero, fractional, negative, and greater-than-one amplitudes. Zero/one sample handling and invalid parameter/rate/dimension checks have independent regressions.

Across all five required native targets, all twenty-three integration tests pass. All tested f32 synthesis samples match C exactly; maximum f64 normalized error is 3.1086244689504383e-15. Normalization uses max(1, sum of absolute tone amplitudes). Scoped acceptance thresholds are 2e-7 for f32 and 2e-14 for f64. The recurrence's original long-signal rounding behavior remains, so these thresholds do not assert equivalence to direct trigonometric evaluation for all lengths.

The WAVE fixtures c-wave-f32.bin and c-wave-f64.bin use tests/reference/wave_oracle.c, the pinned unmodified external/wavfile.c, and gcc -O2 -DFP_TYPE=float/double -I<upstream> driver.c <upstream>/external/wavfile.c -lm. Invoke the executable with the fixture destination path. The original source emits unchecked-fread warnings; no warning-free C build is claimed. Each WAV1 fixture begins with uint32 scalar byte width and record count, then 36 records of uint32 WAVE byte length, raw WAVE bytes, and seven C-decoded scalar samples. All integers are little-endian; reference generation runs on Ubuntu x86_64.

Cases cover PCM 8/16/24/32 and IEEE float 32/64, mono/stereo, and fmt lengths 16/18/40. Extensible cases use standard PCM/float GUIDs. Right-channel samples differ from left to verify the original left-channel selection. Every Rust sample is independently checked against integer normalization or encoded float values. The f32 reference has 140 unchanged and 112 correction-designated samples; the f64 reference has 168 unchanged and 84 correction-designated samples. Correction groups include PCM8 bias, extensible PCM, and f32 PCM32 signed cancellation; some individual values in those groups already agree. These groups are not represented as unchanged-C matches.

Independent tests cover unknown odd chunks containing fake data magic, all truncation positions of a small WAVE, frame budgets, odd final legacy data without padding, empty input, a 128-bit PCM minimum, partial frames, nonzero stream offsets, invalid metadata, duplicate format chunks, path-based reading, injected I/O errors, and borrowed stream survival. The reader supports byte-aligned PCM containers up to 128 bits without fixed-buffer overflow; these additional widths are independently tested at the 128-bit minimum rather than claimed as exhaustive unchanged-C parity. WAVE writing remains pending.

All twenty-eight integration tests passed on Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686. After the final checked-padding-offset change, the five WAVE tests were rerun and passed on all five targets. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied passed.
